title: Invent a style and hold it
summary: See whether a model can invent an unnamed visual style, state its rules, and hold them through a 30-second film including its hardest moment.
originNote: Original task written for this Recipe after Burooj asked that film Recipes taste art style and graphic invention rather than a fixed plot. The subject is left to the model.

setup.instructions: Read fixtures/brief.md. Kitchen supplies the same pinned film toolchain (Node 22, Python, Chromium, FFmpeg and fonts) and compute profile to every compared model. Before Ready, this Recipe's checks must be smoked in that toolchain; this draft is not cookable.

turns.content: Read fixtures/brief.md. Invent and name the style, write STYLE.md, and deliver the film, live player, source, contact sheet and evidence the brief specifies. Make every creative decision yourself and iterate from rendered evidence.

checks.description: Check delivery files, unchanged player, PNG signature, H.264/AAC, 1080 by 1080, 30fps, 900 frames, 30 seconds, complete decode, true peak at or below -0.1 dBTP, evidence shape, and one hardest-moment time inside the film with a note.
STYLE.md begins with the style's name as a heading and states exactly five numbered rules, 1 to 5, each long enough to check a frame against.
Is the style new, or a known look renamed? Can you see each rule in a frame you pick at random? Is the hardest moment really hard, and does it hold? Does the subject grow out of the style?
